CHAPTER 3.1 · LEARNING AREA 3 · JANUARY · FEBRUARY

Coordinates and angles

In Battleships you call “B4”, on a town map you look for “square C7”, and a satnav knows every place by two numbers. The coordinate system turns points into numbers. After that it is about angles: you learn to draw and measure them, to tell their types apart and to discover which angles are always equal when lines intersect.

12 LESSONS3 UNITS4 LABS
WHAT YOU WILL LEARN IN THIS CHAPTER
  • plot and read off points and line segments in the coordinate system
  • draw lines that are parallel and perpendicular to each other
  • draw, measure and label angles and know the types of angle
  • recognise vertically opposite, adjacent, corresponding and alternate angles and justify their properties
CHECK-IN: CAN YOU ALREADY DO THIS?

What is a line called that stops at both ends?

A line segment has two end points, a ray one, a straight line none.

How many right angles does a rectangle have?

one at each corner

By how many degrees does the minute hand turn in a quarter of an hour?

A full turn is 360°, a quarter of that 90°.

UNIT 14 LESSONS

1The coordinate system

If you swap the numbers, you land in a completely different place: (2, 7) is not (7, 2). That is why you need a fixed rule about which number comes first.

A coordinate system has two axes that are perpendicular to each other: the horizontal x-axis and the vertical y-axis. They intersect at the origin O(0, 0). Every point has two coordinates.

KEY POINT · COORDINATES

$P(3, 5)$ means: from the origin go 3 to the right (x-coordinate) and then 5 up (y-coordinate).

Two lines that never intersect are parallel: $g \parallel h$. Two lines that form a right angle are perpendicular to each other: $g \perp h$.

A line segment $\overline{AB}$ has two end points, a ray a starting point, and a straight line has neither a beginning nor an end.

Memory aid: “Along the corridor, then up the stairs”: first to the right, then up.

With the set square: For a perpendicular you put the middle line on the line; for a parallel you slide the set square along an auxiliary line.

INTERACTIVE · POINTS AND LINES IN THE COORDINATE SYSTEM
EXAMPLE 1 · A QUADRILATERAL

Draw A(1, 1), B(6, 1), C(6, 4), D(1, 4) and join them. What do you get?

A rectangle. $\overline{AB}$ and $\overline{DC}$ are horizontal, so parallel; $\overline{AB}$ and $\overline{BC}$ are perpendicular to each other.

a rectangle, 5 squares wide and 3 high

EXAMPLE 2 · THE MIDDLE

Which point lies exactly in the middle of the line segment from P(2, 3) to Q(8, 3)?

Both have the y-coordinate 3. From 2 to 8 is 6 units; the middle is 3 further on than 2.

M(5, 3)

EXERCISES

Draw a coordinate system from 0 to 10 and plot: A(2, 1), B(8, 1), C(8, 7), D(2, 7). Join A to B, B to C, C to D and D to A. What shape do you get?

A square with side length 6.

Which points lie on the x-axis and which on the y-axis? P(0, 4), Q(5, 0), R(0, 0), S(3, 3)

On the x-axis: Q and R. On the y-axis: P and R. S lies on neither axis.

Give the coordinates of three points that lie on a parallel to the x-axis through (0, 4).

All points with the y-coordinate 4, for example (1, 4), (5, 4), (9, 4).

A(1, 2), B(4, 2) and C(4, 6) are three corners of a rectangle. Where is the fourth corner D? How long are the sides?

D(1, 6). The sides are 3 and 4 units long.

Plot the points with fractions and decimals (1 unit = 2 cm): $E(\tfrac12, 1)$, $F(2.5, 1.5)$, $G(1\tfrac34, 0)$.

E lies 1 cm to the right and 2 cm up, F 5 cm to the right and 3 cm up, G 3.5 cm to the right on the x-axis.

The line g passes through (0, 0) and (2, 1). The line h passes through (0, 5) and (1, 3). Draw both. Are they perpendicular to each other? Check with the set square and in the widget.

Yes. g rises 1 for every 2 to the right; h falls 2 for every 1 to the right. If you turn the direction (2, 1) through 90°, you get (−1, 2), the direction of h.

TEST YOURSELF!

What is the x-coordinate of the midpoint of P(2, 3) and Q(8, 3)?

exactly between 2 and 8

Where is the point (4, 0)?

The y-coordinate is 0.

A(1, 2), B(4, 2), C(4, 6) are corners of a rectangle. What is the y-coordinate of D?

D(1, 6)

UNIT 24 LESSONS

2Drawing and measuring angles

A door that is open half as far as when it is fully open forms roughly a right angle with the wall. Good estimators always compare with 90° and 180°.

An angle consists of two arms that start from the same point, the vertex. Angles are labelled with Greek letters: $\alpha$ (alpha), $\beta$ (beta), $\gamma$ (gamma), $\delta$ (delta). They are measured in degrees. A full turn has 360°.

KEY POINT · TYPES OF ANGLE
acute angleless than 90°
right angleexactly 90°
obtuse anglebetween 90° and 180°
straight angleexactly 180°
reflex anglebetween 180° and 360°
full angleexactly 360°

Measuring: put the zero point of the set square on the vertex and the base line on one arm, and read off at the other arm. Use the right scale!

Two scales: There are two rows of numbers on the set square, for example 50 and 130. Estimate beforehand whether the angle is acute or obtuse; then you know which one is right.

Direction: We measure anticlockwise, from the first arm to the second.

INTERACTIVE · MEASURING AND ESTIMATING ANGLES
EXAMPLE 3 · REFLEX

How do you measure an angle of about 250° with a set square that only goes up to 180°?

You measure the smaller angle that is missing to make a full angle, for example 110°, and calculate $360^\circ - 110^\circ$.

250°

EXAMPLE 4 · THE CLOCK

What angle do the hands of a clock form at 4 o’clock?

Between two hour numbers there are $360^\circ \div 12 = 30^\circ$. At 4 o’clock there are 4 gaps in between: $4 \cdot 30^\circ$.

120°, an obtuse angle

EXERCISES

Draw the angles and give their type: $\alpha = 35^\circ$, $\beta = 90^\circ$, $\gamma = 145^\circ$, $\delta = 210^\circ$.

$\alpha$ acute, $\beta$ right, $\gamma$ obtuse, $\delta$ reflex (draw $360^\circ - 210^\circ = 150^\circ$ on the other side).

What angle do the hands of a clock form at a) 3 o’clock   b) 6 o’clock   c) 1 o’clock   d) 8 o’clock (the smaller angle)?

a) 90°   b) 180°   c) 30°   d) 120°

By how many degrees does the minute hand turn in a) 5 minutes   b) 20 minutes   c) an hour? By how many degrees does the hour hand turn in an hour?

a) 30°   b) 120°   c) 360°. The hour hand turns by 30° in an hour.

Estimate five angles in the widget in “Estimate” mode. Note down your estimate and the true value each time. How big was your error on average?

Individual answers. Mean error = sum of the deviations divided by 5. Under 10° is very good.

At 3:30 the minute hand points to the 6. Why is the angle between the hands not 90°? How big is it really?

Where is the hour hand at half past three?

The hour hand is exactly halfway between 3 and 4. To the 6 there are two and a half gaps: $2.5 \cdot 30^\circ = 75^\circ$.

TEST YOURSELF!

What is an angle of 135° called?

between 90° and 180°

What angle do the hands of a clock form at 4 o’clock?

$4 \cdot 30^\circ$

What is missing to make a full angle is 110°. How big is the angle?

$360^\circ - 110^\circ$

UNIT 34 LESSONS

3Angles at intersecting lines

With two intersecting lines, the opposite angles are equal and two angles next to each other add up to 180°. This is true for every pair of lines, not just for your drawings. Why?

KEY POINT · PAIRS OF ANGLES

At two intersecting lines:

  • Adjacent angles lie next to each other and add up to 180°.
  • Vertically opposite angles lie opposite each other and are equal.

If a pair of parallel lines is cut by a third line:

  • Corresponding angles (the same position at both points of intersection, like a stair) are equal.
  • Alternate angles (crosswise on different sides, the shape of a Z) are equal.

Reason for vertically opposite angles: $\alpha_1 + \alpha_2 = 180^\circ$ and $\alpha_2 + \alpha_3 = 180^\circ$. So $\alpha_1$ and $\alpha_3$ must be equal.

Only at parallels! If the two lines are not parallel, corresponding and alternate angles are different sizes. Try it in the widget with “Tilt h”.

INTERACTIVE · PAIRS OF ANGLES
EXAMPLE 5 · ALL ANGLES FROM ONE

Two lines intersect; one angle is $\alpha_1 = 62^\circ$. Calculate the other three.

Adjacent angle: $\alpha_2 = 180^\circ - 62^\circ = 118^\circ$. Vertically opposite angles: $\alpha_3 = 62^\circ$, $\alpha_4 = 118^\circ$.

62°, 118°, 62°, 118°

EXAMPLE 6 · AT PARALLELS

$g \parallel h$ are cut by s. At g, $\alpha_1 = 62^\circ$. How big are $\beta_1$ (corresponding angle) and $\beta_3$?

Corresponding angles at parallels: $\beta_1 = 62^\circ$. $\beta_3$ is vertically opposite $\beta_1$, so also $62^\circ$.

both 62°

EXERCISES

Two lines intersect. One angle is a) 40°   b) 90°   c) 155°. Calculate the other three angles.

a) 140°, 40°, 140°   b) all 90°   c) 25°, 155°, 25°

Draw two parallel lines and a third line that cuts them. Mark a pair of corresponding angles green and a pair of alternate angles blue. Check by measuring.

The measured corresponding angles are equal, and so are the alternate angles.

At parallels one angle is 70°. How many different sizes of angle occur among the eight angles? Which?

Only two: 70° and 110°, each four times.

Use corresponding and vertically opposite angles to explain why alternate angles at parallels are equal.

If $\beta_1$ is the alternate angle to $\alpha_3$: $\beta_1 = \alpha_1$ (corresponding angles at parallels) and $\alpha_1 = \alpha_3$ (vertically opposite angles). So $\beta_1 = \alpha_3$.

TEST YOURSELF!

An angle is 62°. How big is its adjacent angle?

$180^\circ - 62^\circ$

How big is its vertically opposite angle?

Vertically opposite angles are equal.

When are corresponding angles equal?

only at parallels

REVIEW · DEEPEN · CONNECT

Draw the triangle A(1, 1), B(7, 1), C(1, 6). Measure all three angles. What do you notice about their sum?

The angle at A is 90°, the others about 40° and 50°. Together about 180°. More on this in Year 6.

Connecting with chapter 2.1: What fraction of a full turn is an angle of a) 90°   b) 120°   c) 45°   d) 300°?

a) $\tfrac14$   b) $\tfrac13$   c) $\tfrac18$   d) $\tfrac56$

A road crosses two parallel railway tracks at 48°. Behind the tracks a cyclist turns so that he carries on parallel to the first stretch of road. What angle does his path make with the tracks? Make a sketch.

His path is parallel to the road, so it also cuts the tracks at 48° (or the adjacent angle 132°).

EXCURSIONHISTORY

Why does a circle have 360 degrees?

That a full turn has exactly 360 degrees is a very old agreement. Nobody wrote down why. Researchers suspect the reason lies in the sky: in the course of a year the sun moves once all the way round in front of the stars. A year has roughly 360 days. If you divide the circle into 360 parts, the sun moves on by about one part every day.

The astronomers in Babylon divided the path of the sun in this way. The oldest surviving Greek text with 360 parts is by Hypsicles of Alexandria, in the 2nd century BC. The astronomer Hipparchus adopted the division, and through the Greeks it came to us.

360 is also a very practical number: it has 24 factors. You can divide the circle into 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12 and many more equal parts and always get whole degrees.

Sources: Hypsicles: Anaphorikos (On Ascensions), 2nd century BC. O. Neugebauer: A History of Ancient Mathematical Astronomy. Springer, Berlin 1975.
